finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to `URI.open` with no validation, so an attacker can make the server fetch any URL. Reachable targets include cloud metadata (http://169.254.169.254/...), loopback and internal services, and ftp:// URLs. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is a non-blind SSRF.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed unmodified to URI.open, which fetches the URL
The first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: There is no scheme check, host allowlist, IP or DNS check, or redirect handling. The TRUSTED allowlist is defined at line 5 but is not applied on this route. There is no authentication in the app.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes unauthenticated params[:u] directly to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED check exists only on the separate /trusted route (app.rb:14), and app.rb is the only file in the directory, so there is no middleware or other guard.
